fields.AN_Notes: Edited volume coded as one Work. Studientyp Theoretisch follows the predominantly conceptual and argumentative chapters; two chapters carry own data (Plafky et al. usability tests and focus group of an LLM-based case-note prototype; Schlomann draws on the KI-Alter field study), and Holz et al. demonstrate classical NLP on a synthetic case. General_Guidance: Plafky et al. instruct a local Mistral 7B with a fixed case-note structure (Wer, Wann, Wo, Grund, Ablauf, Diskussionsinhalte, Vereinbarungen, fachliche Interpretation, Entscheidung, nächster Termin) and recommend selectable templates per note type. Object_of_Critique rests on Pelzl's analysis of prompting attacks; Learning_Content on Beranek's call to treat prompting as a communicative competence. Bias axes: Age (Schlomann, age discrimination as own chapter argument), Race_Ethnicity (Steiner, AFST and ethnically marginalised children), Socioeconomic (editors' outlook, Allegheny poverty example), Nationality_Migration (editors' bias-audit example and the Dutch child-benefit case), Language_Culture (Swiss German dialect recognition in Plafky et al.), Gender (Beranek's worked example and Schlomann's digital gender gap). Intersectional not coded: the BIPoC-women facial-recognition result is cited from Buolamwini/Gebru without the volume's own combination argument. Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms (editors: addressees deviate from the norm dominating training data), Erasure (Steiner: marginalised groups underrepresented through selection and weighting), Disparate_Performance (own observation that dialects closer to Standard German are recognised better). Discrimination cases (Amazon, Dutch child benefit, Allegheny risk scores, gender-shades) are cited from other work and left uncoded as harm types. Mitigation: training-data analysis, exclusion or synthetic data (Pre_Processing) and bias audit, diverse developer teams, ethics boards, human-in-the-loop and staff training (Organisational_Process), all recommended; AFST evaluation reported by Steiner concerns the tool's side effect on ethnic disparities, not a tested bias mitigation, so status stays Proposed. Bias defined explicitly (Rottkemper, Dummann footnote 6, Löhe). Gender appears only as binary comparison of older men and women and in cited examples. Theory reference: Steiner frames exclusion of marginalised groups through Luhmann's systems-theoretical inclusion/exclusion concept, critical theory and a radical, resistance-oriented concept of inclusion (Rojas).
